## Plotting heatmap of Replogle perturb seq signatures

```{r plotting_replogle_signature}
# R Script: Heatmap Generation from OmicSignatureCollection

# --- 1. Setup and Load Libraries ---
library(tidyverse)     # For data manipulation (dplyr, tidyr)
library(OmicSignature) # To work with OmicSignature objects and collections
library(pheatmap)      # For generating advanced heatmaps

# --- 2. Define Paths ---
combined_collection_input_file <- file.path(
  "/restricted/projectnb/agedisease/projects/challenge2025/results/perturbational_omic_sigs/replogle_2022",
  "Replogle_Perturb_Combined_OmicSignatureCollection.rds"
)
output_heatmap_file <- "combined_omic_signatures_heatmap_smaller_dimensions.pdf"

# --- 3. Load Combined OmicSignatureCollection ---
message("--- Loading Combined OmicSignatureCollection ---")
if (!file.exists(combined_collection_input_file)) {
  stop(paste("Error: The collection file was not found at:", combined_collection_input_file))
}
combined_omic_collection <- readRDS(combined_collection_input_file)
message(paste0("Loaded collection with ", length(combined_omic_collection$OmicSigList), " signatures."))

# --- 4. Extract Signature Scores and Prepare Data for Heatmap ---
message("--- Extracting scores and preparing data matrix ---")

# Initialize an empty list to store data for all signatures
all_signature_data_long <- list()

# Loop through each OmicSignature in the collection
for (sig_key in names(combined_omic_collection$OmicSigList)) {
  omic_sig <- combined_omic_collection$OmicSigList[[sig_key]]
  
  # Get the full signature name (e.g., "GeneX Knockdown Signature - K562")
  full_signature_name <- omic_sig$metadata$signature_name
  
  # Extract the cell line (K562 or RPE1) from the signature name
  cell_line <- str_extract(full_signature_name, "(K562|RPE1)$")
  
  # Ensure we could extract a cell line and the signature data exists
  if (is.na(cell_line) || is.null(omic_sig$signature) || nrow(omic_sig$signature) == 0) {
    warning(paste("Skipping signature due to missing cell line or empty data:", full_signature_name))
    next
  }
  
  # Get the 'signature' data frame which contains top genes and their scores
  sig_df <- omic_sig$signature
  
  # Create a small data frame (tibble) for the current signature
  # We select 'probe_id' as the gene identifier and 'score'
  current_sig_tibble <- tibble(
    signature_name = full_signature_name,
    cell_line = cell_line,
    gene_id = sig_df$probe_id,
    score = sig_df$score
  )
  
  all_signature_data_long[[full_signature_name]] <- current_sig_tibble
}

# Combine all individual signature data frames into one long format table
combined_long_df <- bind_rows(all_signature_data_long)

# Convert the long format data to a wide matrix suitable for a heatmap:
#   - Rows will be the signature names
#   - Columns will be the gene IDs
#   - Values will be the scores
#   - Genes not present in a specific signature will have their score filled with 0
heatmap_matrix_data <- combined_long_df %>%
  # Handle potential duplicate gene_id within a signature (take first score if any)
  distinct(signature_name, gene_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(signature_name, cell_line), # Keep signature_name and cell_line for structure
    names_from = gene_id,                   # Genes become column headers
    values_from = score,                    # Scores fill the matrix cells
    values_fill = 0                         # Fill NA values (gene not in signature) with 0
  )

# Separate the cell line information for row annotations in the heatmap
annotation_df <- heatmap_matrix_data %>%
  dplyr::select(signature_name, cell_line) %>%
  column_to_rownames("signature_name") %>%
  as.data.frame() # pheatmap expects a data.frame for annotations

# Prepare the actual matrix for the heatmap (remove cell_line column)
matrix_for_heatmap <- heatmap_matrix_data %>%
  dplyr::select(-cell_line) %>% # Remove the cell_line column
  column_to_rownames("signature_name") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Check if the matrix is empty after processing
if (nrow(matrix_for_heatmap) == 0 || ncol(matrix_for_heatmap) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No data available to create a heatmap. Please check your OmicSignatureCollection.")
}

message(paste0("Heatmap matrix dimensions: ", nrow(matrix_for_heatmap), " signatures x ", ncol(matrix_for_heatmap), " genes."))

# --- 5. Generate Heatmap with pheatmap ---
message(paste0("--- Generating heatmap and saving to '", output_heatmap_file, "' ---"))

# Define custom colors for the cell line annotation (optional, but good for clarity)
# You can customize these colors further if needed
annotation_colors = list(
  cell_line = c(K562 = "#E41A1C", RPE1 = "#377EB8") # Red for K562, Blue for RPE1
)

# Generate the heatmap
# - `mat`: The matrix of scores
# - `cluster_rows`, `cluster_cols`: Enable clustering for signatures and genes
# - `annotation_row`: Adds a sidebar to the rows, labeling each signature's cell line
# - `annotation_colors`: Applies the custom colors to the annotation sidebar
# - `show_rownames`: Display the full signature names
# - `show_colnames`: Usually too many genes to show names clearly, set to FALSE
# - `main`: Title for the heatmap
# - `filename`: The file path to save the heatmap as a PDF
# - `width`, `height`: Dimensions for the output PDF
pheatmap(
  mat = matrix_for_heatmap,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean", # Common distance metric for rows
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean", # Common distance metric for columns
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",           # Common clustering method
  show_rownames = TRUE,                   # Show signature names (rows)
  show_colnames = FALSE,                  # Hide gene names (columns) as there are usually too many
  annotation_row = annotation_df,         # Add cell line annotation to rows
  annotation_colors = annotation_colors,  # Apply custom colors to cell line annotation
  main = paste0("Signature Scores Heatmap (", nrow(matrix_for_heatmap), " signatures x ", ncol(matrix_for_heatmap), " genes)"),
  fontsize_row = 7,                       # Adjust font size for signature names
  fontsize_col = 5,                       # Adjust font size for gene names if shown
  filename = output_heatmap_file,         # Save the heatmap to a PDF file
  width = 10,                             # Width of the PDF in inches
  height = 20                             # Height of the PDF in inches
)

message("Heatmap generated and saved successfully!")
message("\nScript finished.")

```

```{r FGSEA script: GTEX vs perturb seq replogle}

library(tidyverse) 
library(fgsea)     
library(OmicSignature) 

perturbation_collection_file <- "/restricted/projectnb/agedisease/projects/challenge2025/results/perturbational_omic_sigs/replogle_2022/Replogle_Perturb_Combined_OmicSignatureCollection.rds"

gtex_collection_file <- "/restricted/projectnb/agedisease/projects/challenge2025/data/GTEX/GTEX_aging_omic_col_stat_v114.rds"

output_dir <- "/restricted/projectnb/agedisease/projects/challenge2025/results/perturbational_omic_sigs/replogle_2022/"

# Load OmicSignature Collections
perturb_collection <- readRDS(perturbation_collection_file)
message(paste0("Loaded ", length(perturb_collection$OmicSigList), " perturbation signatures."))

gtex <- readRDS(gtex_collection_file)
message(paste0("Loaded ", length(gtex$OmicSigList), " GTEX aging signatures."))

# Prepare Perturbation Signatures as Gene Sets for fgsea

# Extract probe_ids (genes) from each perturbation signature.
# These will be the "pathways" (gene sets) for fgsea.
perturb_list <- lapply(perturb_collection$OmicSigList, function(x) {
  # Ensure signature data exists and has probe_id
  if (!is.null(x$signature) && "probe_id" %in% names(x$signature)) {
    # Might want to filter genes here based on score if the signatures contain many genes
    return(x$signature$probe_id)
  } else {
    warning(paste("Signature '", x$metadata$signature_name, "' has no 'signature' or 'probe_id'. Skipping."))
    return(character(0)) # Return empty vector for signatures without valid data
  }
})

# Remove any empty gene sets that might have resulted from the warning above
perturbation_gene_sets <- perturb_list[sapply(perturb_list, length) > 0]

# Check if any gene sets were prepared
if (length(perturbation_gene_sets) == 0) {
  stop("No valid perturbation gene sets could be prepared. Check your input data structure.")
}

message(paste0("Prepared ", length(perturbation_gene_sets), " perturbation gene sets for fgsea."))


# Perform fgsea Analysis for each Aging Signature
aging_sigs <- names(gtex$OmicSigList)

message("Starting fgsea analysis across ", length(aging_sigs), " aging signatures...")
res_list <- lapply(aging_sigs, function(aging_nm) {
  age_sig_df <- gtex$OmicSigList[[aging_nm]]$signature

  # Ensure signature data exists and has probe_id and score
  if (is.null(age_sig_df) || !("probe_id" %in% names(age_sig_df)) || !("score" %in% names(age_sig_df))) {
    warning(paste("Aging signature '", aging_nm, "' is missing 'signature', 'probe_id', or 'score'. Skipping."))
    return(NULL) # Return NULL for signatures with missing or incomplete data
  }

  # Create a named, ranked vector of scores for fgsea `stats` argument.
  # fgsea expects gene names as names and scores as values, sorted decreasingly.
  # Genes with higher scores are considered more "upregulated" or significant.
  aging_ranks <- sort(setNames(age_sig_df$score, age_sig_df$probe_id), decreasing = TRUE)

  # Perform fgsea
  fg <- fgsea(pathways = perturbation_gene_sets, # Your perturbation gene sets
              stats    = aging_ranks,          # The ranked aging signature genes
              minSize  = 1,                    # Minimum size of gene set to be considered (adjust as needed)
              maxSize  = 500                   # Maximum size of gene set to be considered (adjust as needed)
  )
  fg$aging_set <- aging_nm # Add the aging signature name to the results table
  return(fg)
})

# Remove any NULL results from the list (for skipped aging signatures)
res_list <- res_list[!sapply(res_list, is.null)]

# Check if any fgsea results were generated
if (length(res_list) == 0) {
  stop("No fgsea results generated. Check for issues in aging signature loading or processing.")
}

# Combine all fgsea results into a single data frame
res_list_df <- do.call(rbind, res_list)

message("fgsea analysis complete. Total results: ", nrow(res_list_df), " rows.")



# Filter and Visualize Significant Results

# Filter for significant results (padj < 0.05) and select top N by absolute NES

if (nrow(res_list_df) == 0) {
  message("No fgsea results to display.")
} else {
  # First, filter for all significant results
  all_significant_results <- res_list_df %>%
    filter(padj < 0.05)

  if (nrow(all_significant_results) == 0) {
    message("No significant interactions (padj < 0.05) found to plot.")
  } else {
    message(paste0("Found ", nrow(all_significant_results), " significant interactions (padj < 0.05)."))

    # --- Plot for Top Upregulated Signatures (Positive NES) ---
    top_upregulated_results <- all_significant_results %>%
      filter(NES > 0) %>% # Select positive NES
      arrange(desc(NES)) %>% # Order by highest NES
      slice(1:min(n(), 20)) # Take top 20, or fewer if less than 20 exist

    if (nrow(top_upregulated_results) > 0) {
      message("Generating plot for top 20 upregulated results...")
      plot_upregulated <- ggplot(top_upregulated_results, aes(x = reorder(pathway, NES), y = aging_set)) +
        geom_point(aes(size  = size, color = NES)) +
        scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Set Size") +
        # Use a single color gradient for positive NES values
        scale_color_gradient(low = "yellow", high = "red", name = "NES") +
        coord_flip() +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)) +
        labs(x = "Perturbation Signature (Gene Set)",
             y = "Aging Signature (Ranked List)",
             title = "Top 20 Upregulated Perturbation Signatures in Aging Signatures (Positive NES)")

      print(plot_upregulated)
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "top_20_upregulated_perturbation_aging_enrichment.pdf"), plot_upregulated, width = 12, height = 8)
      message("Top 20 upregulated plot generated and saved.")

      message("\nTop 20 Upregulated Results (pathway, aging_set, NES, pval, padj, size):")
      print(top_upregulated_results %>% dplyr::select(pathway, aging_set, NES, pval, padj, size))
    } else {
      message("No significant upregulated interactions (NES > 0, padj < 0.05) found to plot.")
    }

    # --- Plot for Top Downregulated Signatures (Negative NES) ---
    top_downregulated_results <- all_significant_results %>%
      filter(NES < 0) %>% # Select negative NES
      arrange(NES) %>% # Order by lowest (most negative) NES
      slice(1:min(n(), 20)) # Take top 20, or fewer if less than 20 exist

    if (nrow(top_downregulated_results) > 0) {
      message("Generating plot for top 20 downregulated results...")
      plot_downregulated <- ggplot(top_downregulated_results, aes(x = reorder(pathway, NES), y = aging_set)) +
        geom_point(aes(size  = size, color = NES)) +
        scale_size_continuous(name = "Gene Set Size") +
        # Use a single color gradient for negative NES values
        scale_color_gradient(low = "darkblue", high = "lightblue", name = "NES") +
        coord_flip() +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
              plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)) +
        labs(x = "Perturbation Signature (Gene Set)",
             y = "Aging Signature (Ranked List)",
             title = "Top 20 Downregulated Perturbation Signatures in Aging Signatures (Negative NES)")

      print(plot_downregulated)
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "top_20_downregulated_perturbation_aging_enrichment.pdf"), plot_downregulated, width = 12, height = 8)
      message("Top 20 downregulated plot generated and saved.")

      message("\nTop 20 Downregulated Results (pathway, aging_set, NES, pval, padj, size):")
      print(top_downregulated_results %>% dplyr::select(pathway, aging_set, NES, pval, padj, size))
    } else {
      message("No significant downregulated interactions (NES < 0, padj < 0.05) found to plot.")
    }
  }
}

```
